title: Attention autotiling regression: safeguards and controlled rollout plan
creator: Priya Nandakumar
description: Summary: During a compiler change that introduced an autotiling heuristic for attention operator codegen, we observed a p95/p99 latency regression on mid-size chat workloads. The change caused the kernel selector to prefer a new tiled attention kernel in scenarios where the legacy fused attention was measurably faster, resulting in sustained capacity pressure and brief throttling incidents for some Dedicated customers.
timeline:
2026-02-12 03:20 UTC - Compiler autotiling commit merged to main (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123)
2026-02-13 09:10 UTC - Canary rollout to hosted-prod region us-west-2 (feature-flagged)
2026-02-13 12:45 UTC - Grafana alerts: p95 generation latency increased by ~48% on svc-chat-infer; earliest customer reports
2026-02-13 13:10 UTC - Ops throttled the canary; rollback triggered for flagged nodes
2026-02-14 07:30 UTC - Post-incident triage meeting; initial hypothesis: autotile thresholds too aggressive for short-sequence distributions
2026-02-18 11:00 UTC - Reproduced regression in lab with sampled production seq-length histogram and batch distributions
2026-02-25 15:00 UTC - Root-cause analysis completed; new mitigations proposed and prototyped
2026-03-05 10:00 UTC - Implemented telemetry changes and safety gates; running staging validation
2026-03-10 16:30 UTC - This follow-up ticket created to track rollout and long-term safeguards
root_cause: The autotiling heuristic used a simplified cost model that overestimated the throughput of the tiled attention kernel for sequence lengths between 64-256 when combined with certain batch size distributions. Because kernel selection happens post-compilation and is influenced by runtime heuristics, the scheduler routed a higher proportion of requests to nodes compiled with the tiled kernel, increasing overall CPU/GPU time per token and causing queueing under peak. A secondary contributing factor was missing regression tests that exercise mid-tail sequence distributions and the absence of a safe fallback to the legacy fused kernel when latency regressed beyond threshold.
actions_taken:
1) Immediate rollback: rolled back autotiling flag across canary hosts and restored previous kernel-defaults (Ops incident reference: INC-2026-022).
2) Hotfix: added a runtime conservative override to prefer fused-attention for detection signatures matching mid-sequence, low-batch scenarios (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8159).
3) Telemetry: added per-kernel selector metrics (+count, p50/p95/p99 latency by kernel_variant, sequence_histogram tag) shipped to Grafana dashboard 'runtime/kernel-selection-v2' (grafana.redwood.internal/d/rt-kernel-selection).
4) Tests: added an e2e benchmark that replays sampled production sequences and batch distributions in CI-emulation (CI job: ci/runtime-autotile-regression).
outstanding_action_items: Finalize cost-model: refine autotile cost heuristic to incorporate measured kernel latencies across seq-length x batch-size grid (owner: Marco Alvarez, estimate: 5)
Safe fallback: implement automated canary rollback when p95 delta > 20% for 10m across any region (owner: SRE team, estimate: 3)
Regression suite: add nightly large-sample regression job that runs mixed sequences against both tiled and fused kernels and fails on >10% p95 regression (owner: QA, estimate: 4)
Rollout plan: prepare a phased rollout with 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% stages and explicit verification gates (owner: Release Eng, due: 2026-03-18)
Dashboarding: add customer-impact view mapping kernel-regressions to customer namespaces and SLA alerts (owner: Observability, estimate: 2)
Documentation: update runtime docs with kernel selection heuristics and override knobs for Dedicated customers (owner: Docs, estimate: 1)
Post-release audit: schedule 72-hour monitoring window after rollout with on-call presence and a rollback playbook (owner: Release Eng)
Edge-case test: create microbenchmarks for KV cache interactions + tiled attention to catch nonlinear interactions (owner: Research/ML Infra)
Backfill telemetry: backfill kernel-variant metrics for the last 30 days from tracing if available (owner: Observability)
Customer comms: prepare customer-facing incident summary and mitigation notes for affected Dedicated accounts (owner: CS)
Automated PR gate: add a lightweight perf-smoke CI gate for compilation-level changes that touch attention codegen (owner: CI)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: tighter autotile heuristics reduce chance of regressions but may leave performance on table for some niche long-sequence workloads. We prioritized customer-facing latency stability over minor tail throughput gains.
Decision: implement conservative autotile cost-model and aggressive safe-fallback for first two release cycles; revisit hybrid strategies after additional telemetry collection.
Review feedback: PM (Elena Ortiz) requested explicit customer-facing controls for Dedicated tenants; Design (Jae Kim) asked for clearer dashboarding to map regressions to feature flags.
Follow-up: consider an A/B style experiment where customers can opt into experimental autotile via tenant-level flag to gather broader telemetry without risking global impact.
Related artifacts: design doc (confluence.redwood.internal/display/RUNTIME/Autotile+Heuristic+Design), production traces (jaeger.redwood.internal/trace/attn-autotile-2026-02-13)
